On the state level the series of warnings, speeches and pronouncements by the Governor and the Attorney General concerning the need for energy conservation all point to a demand for a change in our transportation energy consuming tendencies and the state of Wisconsin's transportation construction policies that encourage increased automobile use. In his remarks to the Merrill Rotary Club on July 10, Attorney General Warren stated,
"What we must now begin to do is to start thinking of ways to get warm or go to work using as few kilowatts or gallons of gasoline as possible. The time has come to change our habits and begin practicing energy conservation and energy frugality.
In line with this statement it is implicit that the Department of Transportation end its policy of meeting every transportation demand by auto drivers.
Even within the Wisconsin Department of Transportation there is recognition of the need for the promotion of energy efficiency and energy conservation. Objective 5 from a document published by the department on September 1, 1971, states,
"A transportation system which is both economical and efficient, attempting to meet all other transportation objectives at the lowest cost possible, and promoting a use of resources for transportation purposes that seeks balance with financial resource allocation in other sectors of the state's economy."
'Minimum disruption of the environment including the natural resource base, of desireable existing neighborhood and community development and of agricultural land patterns."
All of these statements reflect a continuing change in outlook on the role of transportation facilities and the necessity of considering other factors besides decreasing travel time in the decisions of adequate highway facilities.
The Airport Spur as proposed runs contrary to these national, state and departmental goals. If built, the Spur will encourage increased auto use to and from the airport at the expense of more energy efficient modes including the Milwaukee Transport Company service and private limousine service.
Air
Objective 6 states.
The proposed project may contribute to increased deterioration of the air quality in the area. In the statement, the Division of Highways relies on the implementation of clean air devices on new automobiles by 1976. At this point in time with continuing challenges by the auto companies to the rules promulgated by the E.P.A., it is not clear how much of an effect on reducing auto exhaust pollution such rules will have.
